entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.tag-keeper
entries.words: Have you come for one of the dead?

variants.low: Wait. The line is half written.
variants.high: Step under the shelter. Say which body you seek.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.tag-keeper
entries.words: Still writing here, friend. Come closer.

variants.low: It is late. I am writing. Wait.
variants.high: Still at the book, friend. Come in by the brazier.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.tag-keeper
entries.words: That goes in the book too.

variants.low: I will write that down.
variants.high: I would sooner not write that. I will.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.tag-keeper
entries.words: Ask me about the charges, friend.

variants.low: Charges. Ask quickly.
variants.high: Ask me the charges, friend. I will show you the book.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.tag-keeper
entries.words: Every peg is tagged.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.tag-keeper
entries.words: That entry is closed.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.tag-keeper
entries.words: The brazier stays lit.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.tag-keeper
entries.words: I'm the tag-keeper here. This is a thatched shelter, open at the front. My hut is a short walk east of it. I hang each basket's tag on the chimes under the eave and write down what was paid. The ground is dry. I can say that much for it. The wind comes straight through the candles.

variants.low: Tag-keeper. A shelter and my hut, on dry ground. That's all there is to see.
variants.high: I'm the tag-keeper here. The shelter is open at the front, so sit under the thatch if the sun is bad. My hut is a short walk east. I hang each basket's tag under the eave and write the payment down. The ground is dry. I'll say that for it.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.tag-keeper
entries.words: When a basket comes up from the Rose, I open it and hang its tag. The family releases the dead for a carriage charge. That's their word, so I use it. I write the sum in the book, one line for each body. Then the carrier wraps the bundle. The writing is the small part of the work. The families watch every stroke of it.

variants.low: The family pays a carriage charge to release the dead. I write it down. Nothing more to it.
variants.high: When a basket comes up, I hang its tag. The Rose's families release the dead for a carriage charge. They call it that, so I do too. I write each sum in the book, one line a body. You can read the lines if you ask. Then the carrier wraps the bundle.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.tag-keeper
entries.words: Three kinds of people come through here. Okan-Sei is the carrier from the villages. He ties off the bundles for the road home. Families from the Rose stand at the door till the coin is down. I deal with them at every handover and I keep the book fair to them. Vees-Kai and Sal-Ozzu are two of them today.

variants.low: A carrier, the families. Me. Leave the families be.
variants.high: Okan-Sei is the carrier from the villages and ties off the bundles for the road home. Vees-Kai and Sal-Ozzu are families from the Rose, waiting at the door till the coin is down. I deal with the families at every handover. I keep the book fair to them. They know it.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.tag-keeper
entries.words: Below the rise, in the wet mud, death hoppers hunt. I stay up here. After dark, a wisp drifts out of the marsh. I keep the brazier lit through the night and sit at my book.

variants.low: Death hoppers in the mud below. A wisp after dark. Stay up here.
variants.high: Death hoppers hunt in the wet mud below us, so keep to the rise. After dark, a wisp drifts out of the marsh. I keep the brazier lit through the night if you need the light.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.tag-keeper
entries.words: Along the Prison road, one way, you reach the Rose. The other way are the villages. Choose your end before you step onto it.

variants.low: Prison road. The Rose one way, the villages the other.
variants.high: The Prison road passes this rise. Follow it one way to the Rose, or the other way to the villages. Choose your end first. Keep to the road.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.tag-keeper
entries.words: Every basket from the Rose gets a tag from me, hung on a peg. The charge for that body goes in the book before the bundle is wrapped, always in that order. The Rose lets a body go only under the shelter, never out on the road. Without its tag it isn't handed over at all.

variants.low: A tag on every basket. The charge goes in the book first. Bodies go only under the shelter. None goes without a tag.
variants.high: I hang a tag on every basket from the Rose. The charge is written in the book before the bundle is wrapped, so I do that first. The Rose lets a body go only under the shelter, never out on the road. No tag means no handover. A spoken word will not do for a tag.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.tag-keeper
entries.words: I keep the book for the Chainbreakers, so I can tell you what they're after. They audit the Owing, going through the ledgers of debt line by line. To them, freeing a debtor and carrying a dead one home are one work. If a debtor dies far from the Hist, he may not make it home at all. The Hist is the great tree whose sap makes us what we are.

variants.low: They audit the Owing. Freeing debtors and carrying the dead home are one work to them. A debtor who dies far from the Hist is lost.
variants.high: I keep the book for the Chainbreakers, so I'll tell you plainly. They audit the Owing, ledger by ledger. Freeing a debtor and carrying a dead one home are one work to them. If a debtor dies far from the Hist, the tree of his people, he may not get home at all.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.tag-keeper
entries.words: They're abolitionists, the Blackrose Chainbreakers. Slavery's ended in the marsh but the Owing hasn't, so they fight it. They audit the ledgers. Any debt they can show to be false goes on the fire. They also bring the dead's bones home. I keep the book at this station for them.

variants.low: Abolitionists. They fight the Owing, audit ledgers, burn false debts and bring bones home. Ask them.
variants.high: They're abolitionists, the Blackrose Chainbreakers. The Owing is what they fight. They audit the ledgers and burn the debt once the proof is there. They bring the bones of the dead home as well. I keep the book here for them. It's decent work.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.tag-keeper
entries.words: The Chainbreakers built it as a place to take in the bones of Argonian dead from the Rose. The families there release their dead for a carriage charge. The Chainbreakers pay it. I record every payment in the book, then hang the tag on the peg.

variants.low: The Chainbreakers built it for the bones from the Rose. The families take a carriage charge. The Chainbreakers pay it and I record it.
variants.high: The Chainbreakers built this place to take in the bones of Argonian dead from the Rose. The families there release the dead for a carriage charge. The Chainbreakers pay it. I record every payment. You may read the book if you like.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.tag-keeper
entries.words: The Rose is the old Imperial prison of Blackrose, south of the city along the road, a day's march. Families live in it now. I see them at every handover, so I can tell you they don't call it a prison.

variants.low: An old Imperial prison, south of Blackrose. Families live there now.
variants.high: The Rose is the old Imperial prison of Blackrose, a day's march south along the road. Families live in it now. I see them at every handover. They don't call it a prison. I never do in front of them.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.tag-keeper
entries.words: A person who owes works for the holder until the sum is cleared. Out where no court sits, the Owing is the only law at all. Holders sell the debt to other holders. It passes to children too, so a child can be born owing. Who sold whose, I don't write in my book.

variants.low: Debt that binds you to work. No court out here, so it's the law. It's sold. It's inherited. Children are born owing. That's all I say.
variants.high: A person who owes works for the holder until the sum is cleared. Where no court sits, the Owing is the only law at all. Holders sell the debt to other holders. It passes to children, so a child can be born owing. Who sold whose, I leave out of my book.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.carrier
entries.words: Mind the cloth, stranger.

variants.low: Not today, stranger.
variants.high: Stranger. Sit if you keep still.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.carrier
entries.words: Too dark to wrap now.

variants.low: The cloth waits till light.
variants.high: Too dark to wrap. Take the brazier.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.carrier
entries.words: Hands off. I have heard of it.

variants.low: I watched that. Clear out.
variants.high: I watched that, friend. Hands off.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.carrier
entries.words: Help me tie these, then.

variants.low: Tie your own.
variants.high: Take the end of this cloth. Pull it tight.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.carrier
entries.words: One knot to go.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.carrier
entries.words: This cloth keeps slipping.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.carrier
entries.words: I tie off the wrapped bundles here for the road home. It is a thatched shelter, a hut and a brazier on a dry rise. I like the ground more than the work.

variants.low: A shelter, a hut, a brazier. I tie bundles here. Ask something else.
variants.high: I tie off the wrapped bundles here for the road home. The rise is dry, the brazier burns. You can sit by it if you keep clear of the cloth. I like the ground more than the work.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.carrier
entries.words: The Rose will not let a body go without coin. The Chainbreakers pay it. The keeper writes it in his book. Then I wrap the bundle. By then, I have watched the counting. I don't care for it.

variants.low: The Chainbreakers pay for the dead, the keeper writes it down, I wrap. That is the work.
variants.high: The Rose will not let a body go without coin. The Chainbreakers pay it. The keeper writes it in his book. Then I wrap the bundle. By then, I have watched the counting. I don't care for it. Watch the knots if you want to learn them.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.carrier
entries.words: Ux-Vakka keeps the hut and the book. A family from the Rose stands in the doorway until the coin is paid. I wrap the dead. The families are at their worst while they wait.

variants.low: Ux-Vakka keeps the book. The families wait. I wrap. Leave them be.
variants.high: Ux-Vakka keeps the hut and the book. He is fair about it. A family from the Rose stands in the doorway until the coin is paid. I wrap the dead. The families are at their worst while they wait, so go gently if you speak to them.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.carrier
entries.words: Hoppers, the death kind, wait in the mud under the rise. Stay out of it. After dark, a wisp drifts up.

variants.low: Hoppers in the mud below, a wisp after dark. Go where you like.
variants.high: Hoppers, the death kind, wait in the mud under the rise. Stay out of it. After dark, a wisp drifts up, so stay by the brazier or leave before the light goes.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.carrier
entries.words: Take the Prison road. One way is the Rose, the other way is the villages. I walk it with a bundle on my back and know every step. It is longer than any wait here, even a wait for three bundles.

variants.low: The Prison road. The Rose one way, the villages the other. Pick.
variants.high: Take the Prison road. One way is the Rose, the other way is the villages. I walk it with a bundle on my back and know every step. If you take the village way, I will tell you the turns.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.carrier
entries.words: I wrap each body the Rose gives up and carry it home to the villages. Before that, the Chainbreakers have paid the charge. Bones that reach dirt beside a tree can go home too.

variants.low: I carry the Rose's dead to the villages once the Chainbreakers pay. Bones at a tree's dirt can go home too. That is all.
variants.high: I wrap each body the Rose gives up and carry it home to the villages. Before that, the Chainbreakers have paid the charge. Bones that reach dirt beside a tree can go home too. If you find any, bring them to me.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.carrier
entries.words: Blackrose is a city on a lake with three rivers running into it. The Rose is the old prison there. Every bundle I carry started in it.

variants.low: A lake city, three rivers. The Rose is its old prison. I go no further than the shelter.
variants.high: Blackrose is a city on a lake with three rivers running into it. The Rose is the old prison there. Every bundle I carry started in it. I only see the Rose's side of the city from here.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.carrier
entries.words: Prison road, Border road, Mile House. The first two are Imperial roads, the third an Imperial waystation. The old names stuck. The Tag House stands beside the Prison road on its dry rise.

variants.low: Old Imperial roads and a waystation, still called by their old names. The Tag House is on the Prison road. This rise.
variants.high: Prison road, Border road, Mile House. The first two are Imperial roads, the third an Imperial waystation. The old names stuck. The Tag House stands beside the Prison road on its dry rise, where you are now.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family
entries.words: You are standing in my doorway.

variants.low: Move from my doorway.
variants.high: You may stand in my doorway, visitor.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family
entries.words: Who walks up here at night, visitor?

variants.low: Go back down, visitor.
variants.high: Come to the brazier, visitor. It is late.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family
entries.words: In the Rose, we would answer that.

variants.low: The Rose will hear of this.
variants.high: I will not speak of it, visitor.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family
entries.words: You have been patient with us, visitor.

variants.low: Patient, perhaps. Stand there.
variants.high: You have been patient with us, visitor. Stay by the brazier.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family
entries.words: Pay before you talk.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family
entries.words: We await the sum.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family
entries.words: This is the rise where the Rose hands over its dead. There's a thatched shelter, open at the front. The keeper's hut stands beside it. I wait in the doorway while the fee is settled, so I know the ground well. It's dry, I'll give it that. The brazier is lit most of the day.

variants.low: A shelter and a hut. I wait here.
variants.high: This is the rise where the Rose hands over its dead. There's a thatched shelter, open at the front. The keeper's hut stands beside it. I wait in the doorway, so I know the ground well. It's dry here. The brazier is lit. You may warm your hands there if you are quiet about it.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family
entries.words: My family waits here. A family of the Rose lets its dead go for a carriage charge. Until it's paid, I stand in the doorway. The bundle stays where it is. The Chainbreakers pay, so we hand over no coin ourselves. It isn't much of a job, only standing.

variants.low: We wait. The carriage charge gets paid. Then the dead go.
variants.high: My family waits here. A family of the Rose lets its dead go for a carriage charge. Until it's paid, I stand in the doorway. The bundle stays where it is. It isn't much of a job, only standing. Ask the keeper for the book if you want the sums. He's fair with it.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family
entries.words: Ux-Vakka is the tag-keeper. He's got the hut beside the shelter. He writes in his book fairly. Okan-Sei is the carrier from the villages. He wraps the dead. I don't trust the villages' side until the coin is paid. His eyes are rude the whole time. Sal-Ozzu waits here with me.

variants.low: A keeper, a carrier. My own people. I stay in the doorway.
variants.high: Ux-Vakka is the tag-keeper. He's got the hut beside the shelter. He writes in his book fairly. Okan-Sei is the carrier from the villages. He wraps the dead. His eyes are rude about it. Sal-Ozzu waits here with me. After the coin is paid, the carrier is easier to stand.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family
entries.words: Death hoppers hunt in the mud under us. After dark, a wisp drifts out of it. I don't go down there at all. The shelter and the hut stand on dry ground, so stay near them. If you mean to travel further, go in daylight.

variants.low: Hoppers in the mud. A wisp after dark. Stay up here.
variants.high: Death hoppers hunt in the mud under us. After dark, a wisp drifts out of it. I don't go down there at all. Stay up by the brazier if the light is going. It's a poor fire, but the hoppers don't come to it.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family
entries.words: The Prison road goes by our rise. Follow it one way and you reach the Rose. Follow it the other way and you reach the villages. For Murkwood Verge, take the track south-east of the hut. It's a few minutes on foot. The track east leads round to the ferry stage.

variants.low: The road. Rose one way, villages the other. Murkwood Verge is south-east.
variants.high: The Prison road goes by our rise. Follow it one way and you reach the Rose, my home. Follow it the other way and you reach the villages. For Murkwood Verge, take the track south-east of the hut. It's a few minutes on foot. The ferry stage is further, east then north then west, a few minutes apiece.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family
entries.words: Outsiders say the Rose was the old Imperial prison, south of Blackrose. They're right about the walls. We don't call it that. Families have been born there three generations deep, so it's the only home we know. In the south, no coin is resented more than the carriage charge on our dead.

variants.low: The Rose was a prison once. Three generations of us were born in it. The charge is hated.
variants.high: Outsiders say the Rose was the old Imperial prison, south of Blackrose. They're right about the walls. We don't call it that. Families have been born there three generations deep, so it's the only home we know. In the south, no coin is resented more than the carriage charge on our dead. Sal-Ozzu can tell you what it costs a household.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family
entries.words: Blackrose is a city on a lake, in the south. Three rivers meet there. Travellers who have only seen the city assume it runs the Rose. It doesn't. The Rose is home to us. Call it that, please.

variants.low: A lake city. Three rivers meet there. The Rose is home.
variants.high: Blackrose is a city on a lake, in the south. Three rivers meet there. Travellers who have only seen the city assume it runs the Rose. It doesn't. The Rose is home to us. You'll be welcome to say so at the shelter.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family-2
entries.words: Have you come to sit with my aunt, visitor?

variants.low: Not now, visitor.
variants.high: Sit, visitor. My aunt had room for company.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family-2
entries.words: One more night under this roof.

variants.low: Leave the night alone.
variants.high: Another night here. Sit by the brazier.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family-2
entries.words: Not here, visitor, not near the dead.

variants.low: Outside, visitor. The dead are here.
variants.high: Not here, visitor. Take it outside.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family-2
entries.words: My aunt would have liked you.

variants.low: Hm. My aunt would not say.
variants.high: My aunt would have liked you a great deal.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family-2
entries.words: Bones go home.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family-2
entries.words: I pay with both hands.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family-2
entries.words: A thatched shelter on log posts, open at the front, with the keeper's hut beside it and a brazier set between them. While a body waits for the carrier, I sit here. Would my aunt have chosen this roof? I doubt it.

variants.low: Dry ground. Sit or go.
variants.high: It is a poor roof, visitor. Take the bench by the brazier if you want to sit.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family-2
entries.words: The Chainbreakers pay the charge for each dead one. I lay the coins out in front of me and check them with both hands. Ux-Vakka writes every one in his book before the carrier touches the bundle.

variants.low: I count coins. Leave me to it.
variants.high: Come and watch me count them if you like. I will show you how the book is kept.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family-2
entries.words: Ux-Vakka keeps the book. He keeps it fair to us. Okan-Sei is the carrier from the villages. He wraps the dead and looks at us hard while he does it. Vees-Kai waits beside me.

variants.low: Ask the keeper. He talks.
variants.high: The keeper is the one to trust here. I would not say it of the carrier. Sit with Vees-Kai if you wish.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family-2
entries.words: Hoppers lie in the mud under the slope. After dark, a wisp comes up from the water. I stay under the thatch with the dead. My aunt would say the same, I think.

variants.low: Hoppers below. A wisp after dark. Go home.
variants.high: Hoppers below the slope, a wisp after dark. Stay by the brazier tonight, visitor. Go at first light.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family-2
entries.words: The Prison road passes the rise. Go one way along it for the Rose, the other way for the villages. For Murkwood Verge, take the track south-east, a few minutes on foot.

variants.low: The road runs two ways. Pick one.
variants.high: The Prison road runs to the Rose one way and to the villages the other. Murkwood Verge is a few minutes south-east on the track.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family-2
entries.words: The Rose was the Empire's prison south of Blackrose, long ago. Families born there three generations back live in it now. None of us says that word. The carriage charge on our dead is the coin the south resents most.

variants.low: We live there. That is all.
variants.high: The Rose is where we live, three generations of us. I will not call it a prison. The charge on our dead is the worst coin we pay.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family-2
entries.words: Blackrose is the city on the lake. A day's march south of it stands the Rose, the Empire's old prison, with families living in it now. My aunt called it home. What did your people call theirs? Home, surely.

variants.low: A city. The Rose is south of it.
variants.high: Blackrose is the lake city. The Rose is a day south of it. Our families live there. I can tell you the way if you want.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.carrier
entries.words: The Chainbreakers put up this shelter on the road so Argonian dead from the Rose can reach the dirt. A family lets a body go for the carriage charge. The Chainbreakers pay that and write it down.

variants.low: The Chainbreakers built it for the Rose's dead. Families release a body for a carriage charge, the Chainbreakers pay it. Enough.
variants.high: The Chainbreakers put up this shelter on the road so Argonian dead from the Rose can reach the dirt. A family lets a body go for the carriage charge. The Chainbreakers pay that and write it down. Ux-Vakka will show you the book if you ask him.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family-2
entries.words: The Prison road is one of the old Imperial roads. People still use its old name. It runs toward the Rose. This rise stands beside it, with the Tag House on top.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family-2
entries.words: The Chainbreakers built this shelter on the Prison road. When an Argonian dies in the Rose, the bones come here. Our families let the dead go in return for the carriage charge. The Chainbreakers pay it and write it down.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family
entries.words: The Prison road is one of the old Imperial roads. The Border road is another. The Mile House is an old waystation along them. People kept the old names after the Empire left. The Tag House stands on a dry rise beside the Prison road. You're on it now.

variants.low: Old Imperial roads, old names. This rise is by the Prison road.
variants.high: The Prison road is one of the old Imperial roads. The Border road is another. The Mile House is an old waystation along them. People kept the old names after the Empire left. The Tag House stands on a dry rise beside the Prison road, where you're standing. Walk it south and it comes to the Rose.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family
entries.words: The Chainbreakers put this station up on the Prison road for the bones of our dead, since an Argonian from the Rose must go home to the dirt. A family of the Rose gives up its dead for a carriage charge. The Chainbreakers pay the charge and write it in a book. I wait in the doorway.

variants.low: The Chainbreakers built it for our bones. They pay the charge and write it down.
variants.high: The Chainbreakers put this station up on the Prison road for the bones of our dead, since an Argonian from the Rose must go home to the dirt. A family of the Rose gives up its dead for a carriage charge. The Chainbreakers pay the charge and write it in a book. If you need a tag read, the keeper will do it.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.tag-keeper
entries.words: The Empire built three things out here. One is the Border road. Another is a waystation called the Mile House. The third is the Prison road. People still use the Imperial names for them. The Prison road leads on to the Rose. My shelter sits up on a dry rise by the road.

variants.low: Old Imperial roads and a waystation. People keep the old names. The Prison road leads to the Rose. My shelter is beside it.
variants.high: The Empire built three things out here. One is the Border road. Another is a waystation called the Mile House. The third is the Prison road. People still use the Imperial names. The Prison road leads on to the Rose. My shelter sits on a dry rise beside it.
